head.name: @fzlt/core/input
head.lead: One controller for keys, pointer and a touch stick, mapped to named intents. Listeners only record; the engine's read phase latches edges and measures the target, so a step sees a stable snapshot. Keys typed into the host page's fields (or inside [data-fizlet-ignore]) never count. Keys, the pointer, press() and steer() wake a settled engine. Held state is dropped on window blur, when the engine pauses, on dispose() and on destroy: nothing stays stuck. hit (an intent or the pointer): a press is seen by exactly one fixed step, the first step after it, even when that comes frames later (0-step frames while catching up) and never again in the same frame's later steps. Outside a step (read, render), hit is true for the one frame whose read latched it. Presses between two steps count once.

items.doc: Gamepads into a controls() controller: mapped buttons press their intents (down from half a pull), the left stick steers the controller's stick, both past the dead zone. It polls in the controller's read phase, before the edges latch, and only while a pad is connected: a page without one never calls getGamepads() per frame. Pads have no events for buttons, so a settled engine is not polled: a pad connecting wakes it, and a game that settles between rounds wakes it from its own start key. Zero allocation per read. stop() removes it (listeners, polling, held intents and the stick).
